items.headline: October 26 agenda listed three-townhome proposal at 536 Hawthorn Avenue
items.summary: The Planning Commission's October 26 agenda listed a 6 p.m. study session on a proposal to demolish a 1,360-square-foot duplex on a 0.29-acre R-3 lot and build three townhome-style condominiums in one two-story building. The application also includes a tentative parcel map to split the parcel into three lots.

items.headline: Citywide residential parking rules rewrite: continuance to Nov. 9 requested
items.summary: The October 26 Planning Commission agenda carried a request to continue to November 9 a recommendation to the City Council on repealing and replacing Sunnyvale's parking chapter (19.46). The proposed ordinance would also amend parking provisions in the Downtown, Lawrence Station, and El Camino Real specific plan districts, as well as the Dual Urban Opportunity Housing chapter.

items.headline: Pruneyard asks to push back office tower deadlines to 2031
items.summary: The October 20 City Council agenda listed a public hearing on the Pruneyard Center Association's request to extend the phasing deadlines for Phases 3 and 4 to December 31, 2031. Those phases include a five-story office building, parking structure expansions and additional commercial buildings at S. Bascom Ave and E. Campbell Ave. The request also covers extending the tentative parcel map that would create a fourth parcel for the office building. The agenda said the Planning Commission recommends the council approve it.

items.headline: Council agenda: child care partnership at Cubberley and Caltrain funding scenario
items.summary: The October 19 City Council agenda listed approval of a letter of intent with Palo Alto Community Child Care for a long-term public-private partnership to expand child care at the Cubberley site. It also listed a Caltrain presentation on a framework for a "No External Funding Scenario" and $15,000 from Council Contingency for the Know Your Neighbors Grant Program.

items.headline: 692,634-square-foot Walsh Avenue proposal: November 18 continuance listed on agenda
items.summary: The October 14 Development Review Hearing agenda listed a continuance to November 18, 2026, for architectural review of a three-story office building at 2300 and 2350 Walsh Avenue. The plan would demolish the existing structures and add 2,050 below-grade parking stalls, a solar trellis over surface parking, and a pedestrian bridge across Walsh Avenue.

items.headline: Two small homes proposed to replace one house on Franklin Street
items.summary: The October 14 Development Review Hearing agenda listed an architectural review to demolish a single-family house and detached garage at 575 Franklin Street. In their place would go a two-story 1,462-square-foot home and a one-story 778-square-foot home. The site is within 200 feet of a historic resource inventory property.
